analysis_review: I should preface this review by saying that I’ve only been playing this game for the past year or so, so whilst there are a considerable number of players who have a legitimate gripe about this game being stuck in early-access Hell, I can’t count myself amongst them, although that being said, I do see their side of things. If you love ghost hunting or just the paranormal in general, this game is for you. And for those that aren’t, don’t worry; it’s a great game to play with friends, especially if you’re looking for something spooky, on the cheaper side, and with great replayability. Recent updates have been… janky to say the least, and there are inconsistencies with the mechanics that do need addressing. However, the team behind it is actively adding new updates/events pretty consistently, so some turbulence is to be expected. The new character model system has been especially devicive, but don’t let that put you off; as long as you’re not expecting in-depth character customization, you should be fine. At the end of the day, for £16, I feel I’ve gotten way more than my money’s worth out of it and will continue to do so. I hope you do too!

Phasmophobia is exactly the kind of ghost-hunting chaos I want. The problem is that I have no friends to play it with. Which is rude, because this game is clearly built for group panic. I want to walk into a haunted house with a flashlight, a dream, and the confidence of someone who has watched way too much Sam and Colby. I want to ask ghosts disrespectful questions, immediately regret it, and then scream because something moved in the kitchen. The whole setup is so good. You gather evidence, use equipment, watch for signs, try to figure out what kind of ghost you are dealing with, and then attempt to leave before it turns your investigation into a funeral announcement. It is creepy, funny, stressful, and so much better when everyone is panicking together. One person is trying to be serious. One person is already hiding in the van. One person is yelling the ghost’s name like they have never heard of consequences. That is the dream. Even without a full group, I still love the idea of it. The atmosphere is tense, the ghost mechanics are fun, and every investigation feels like it could go from “we are professionals” to “absolutely not, goodbye” in half a second. Phasmophobia lets me live my Sam and Colby dreams, or at least it would if my friends would get their lives together and play with me. Until then, I am just standing outside the haunted house with equipment, trust issues, and no backup.

Phasmophobia: A Masterclass in Shared Terror If you had told me a few years ago that I’d spend my weekends willingly walking into dark, haunted houses just to get mocked by a demon via a Spirit Box, I would have called you crazy. Yet, here I am, utterly hooked on Phasmophobia. While the game is brilliant as a solo horror experience, it truly transcends into something special when played in co-op. I’ve been playing exclusively with my brother, and it has easily become our favorite gaming ritual. The Joy of Custom Terrors What keeps Phasmophobia so incredibly fresh—even after hours of hunting—is how adaptable it is. Once you get a handle on the basic mechanics, the game gives you the freedom to make your own fun. My brother and I have started cooking up our own custom challenges to test our nerves, like: The "No Flashlight" Challenge: Relying strictly on candles and glowsticks to navigate a massive asylum. The Speed-Run: Trying to identify the ghost and escape within five minutes. The sandbox nature of the difficulty settings allows you to tweak the game to perfectly match your skill level, keeping the tension sky-high. The Thrill of the Hunt (and the Loot) Beyond just surviving, there is a genuine addiction to searching the maps for cursed possessions. There is nothing quite like the chaotic adrenaline rush of finding a deck of Tarot Cards. The dynamic changes instantly: do we play it safe, or do we risk pulling a High Priestess (or worse, the Death card) just for the thrill of it? Hunting down these items, filling up the investigation journal, and snapping perfect photos of the paranormal feels less like a repetitive loop and more like a genuine, eerie treasure hunt. The Verdict Phasmophobia balances genuine, heart-pounding dread with incredible cooperative gameplay. The sound design is top-tier (hearing a ghost breathe right in your ear will never not make you jump), and the proximity chat creates unforgettable moments of panic and comedy. If you have a dedicated gaming partner—like a sibling who is willing to use you as ghost bait—this game is an absolute must-play. It’s scary, it’s chaotic, and it’s some of the most fun you can have in the dark.
